articles.title: P&G beats estimates as price hikes haven't hurt demand yet
articles.summary: P&G earnings surprise despite macro pressures.
articles.body:
Procter & Gamble's ( PG ) price hikes aren't crushing a consumer base dealing with higher inflation, yet.

The Tide maker delivered sales and profit upside for its fiscal first quarter on Thursday. The company maintained its full-year sales and profit outlooks.

"The US consumer is remarkably resilient," P&G CFO Andre Schulten told Yahoo Finance.

Schulten said the business is being powered by higher income households, while the lower end is being more cautious.

P&G shares rose 2% in pre-market trading.

Net sales: $23.28 billion, +4% from the prior year vs. $22.82 billion estimate

Organic sales growth: +4% vs. +1.96% estimate Beauty segment organic revenue growth: +5.4% vs. +3.58% estimate Grooming segment organic revenue growth: +4.5% vs. +0.7% estimate Healthcare segment organic revenue growth: +2.7% vs. +2.51% estimate Fabric and home care segment organic revenue growth: +4.8% vs. +2.35% estimate Baby, feminine, and family care segment organic revenue growth: +3% vs. +0.99% estimate

Organic sales growth: +4% vs. +1.96% estimate

Beauty segment organic revenue growth: +5.4% vs. +3.58% estimate

Grooming segment organic revenue growth: +4.5% vs. +0.7% estimate

Healthcare segment organic revenue growth: +2.7% vs. +2.51% estimate

Fabric and home care segment organic revenue growth: +4.8% vs. +2.35% estimate

Baby, feminine, and family care segment organic revenue growth: +3% vs. +0.99% estimate

Adjusted earnings per share: $2.00, +1% from the prior year vs. $1.89 estimate

What else caught our attention: A sustained outlook

P&G reiterated organic sales growth of 1% to 3% for its fiscal year.

For the year, earnings are still expected to range from $6.89 to $7.11. Analysts were looking for fiscal year 2027 organic revenue growth of 2.19% and core earnings per share of $6.98.

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

articles.title: Meta's new nonvoting shares create an overhang — and Wall Street wants it gone
articles.summary: Meta should move fast on its new share sale, Wall Street says.
articles.body:
Meta ( META ) has created a new overhang on its stock that Wall Street wasn't expecting when it established a new class of stock.

The Street's advice to Mark Zuckerberg and his team: Issue the stock fast so the focus can return to the clear product momentum the company is enjoying with its new Muse AI agent .

"The sooner the better in our view as it would remove the overhang and the Street now knows it will have non-voting shares in Jan'27, and Meta can still do a substantial equity raise before then without even coming close to impacting Mark's voting control," JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth said.

Meta announced late Wednesday that it is establishing a new class of nonvoting Class C common stock, which effectively serves as a 2-for-1 stock split.

Under the scheme — in part designed to keep founder Mark Zuckerberg working in California as the 5% billionaire's tax looms — existing shareholders will receive one new nonvoting Class C share for every Class A or Class B share they hold. Trading is slated to begin in January 2027.

Issuing nonvoting stock allows Zuckerberg to raise external capital for Meta's AI build-out without diluting his personal voting control over the tech giant.

The news took some air out of the balloon on what was an impressive quarter for Meta amid signs that its AI investments are paying off.

Meta's core advertising business reported a 26% increase in total revenue to $64.6 billion, powered by AI-driven recommendations, higher ad volume, and rising ad prices.

GAAP earnings per share came in at $3.83 versus analyst estimates of $3.56.

Meta stock fell 2% in premarket trading on Thursday.

"Net/net, some near-term noise in Meta shares, but we're encouraged by core Advertising and Meta's outlook for strong overall revenue growth in 2027, and the path to superintelligence is increasingly clear w/the Muse series of models & products," Anmuth said.

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

articles.title: Apple's $1,999 iPhone Duo hits stores Friday amid limited supplies
articles.summary: The iPhone Duo goes on sale Friday, but in-store supplies will be limited.
articles.body:
Apple's ( AAPL ) iPhone Duo goes on sale Friday, but you may be hard-pressed to get your hands on one.

Preorders for the company's first foldable smartphone sold out almost immediately last week, with delivery times pushed out well into late January.

As for getting a Duo on launch day, either you're already in line at an Apple Store, or you'll need to get extremely lucky.

The company said that while it has allocated some supply for walk-in customers, it expects that supply to sell out quickly.

"On Friday morning, our teams look forward to welcoming customers at Apple Stores to experience iPhone Duo and the incredible iPhone line-up for themselves," Apple said in a statement.

"Apple Stores will have limited iPhone Duo available for walk-in customers, and we're working hard to get this revolutionary new product into customers' hands as quickly as possible."

At least some of the preorder madness comes down to scalpers hawking the foldable iPhone on sites like eBay at a stiff markup.

While the iPhone Duo starts at $1,999, sellers are asking for upwards of $4,000 for the pricey smartphone.

The Duo is one of Apple's most anticipated products in years. The biggest update to the company's most important device since it launched in 2007, the iPhone Duo could help raise the iPhone's average selling price, boosting Apple's bottom line.

The iPhone represented $209.58 billion of Apple's $416.16 billion in total revenue in 2025. That's well ahead of the company's second-largest business segment, Services, which brought in $109.15 billion.

The Duo also comes as Apple revamps its iPhone release schedule. Rather than debuting its full lineup of phones at its annual September event last month, Apple revealed only its top-tier smartphones, including the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max.

The company is widely expected to unveil its standard iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 early next year. That should help even out the lumpiness in Apple's seasonal sales and provide a clearer picture of which devices consumers are purchasing.

Email Daniel Howley at dhowley@yahoofinance.com. Follow him on Twitter at @DanielHowley .

articles.title: Elon Musk says Tesla's Optimus robot needs to learn like a toddler
articles.summary: The Tesla CEO offered a fresh reminder that getting Optimus to behave like a human is no easy task.
articles.body:
Tesla ( TSLA ) CEO Elon Musk reminded investors this past summer that making thumbs for the Optimus humanoid robot would be no easy task.

Now he's out with a fresh reminder that getting Optimus to behave like a human out in the wild is also no easy task. Two reminders in under six months will likely cause Wall Street to dial back its sales estimates for Optimus in the medium term.

It appears Tesla is doing something similar — pulling back its $25 billion full-year capital expenditures commitment to $20 billion to ensure the humanoids the company delivers are highly usable.

"A big difference with Optimus versus the cars is we don't have this vast fleet of cars from which we can gather training data," Musk said on his late Wednesday earnings call . "With Optimus, we have to bootstrap it by making the robots and having them do self-play, which is really how a human learns to navigate the world. You can see this when you have a toddler, and they grow up, and initially, they're sort of wobbly, and they don't know how to do things. Eventually they learn to wipe their own ass, which is a big milestone. As anyone who's had kids knows. Then they learn to read and do all sorts of things and be able to do these things. They learn this by playing. We actually need Optimus to play at scale in order to have it be really good at tasks in the real world."

Tesla ended production of its flagship Model S and Model X vehicles at its Fremont, Calif., factory this past spring, specifically to make room for Optimus humanoid robot production — a stunning strategic pivot that tells you how all-in Musk is on this program.

The latest version, Optimus V3, stands 5'8" tall, weighs 125 pounds, runs on Tesla's new AI5 chip with roughly five times the memory bandwidth of its predecessor, and is powered by xAI's Grok for voice.

Production began at the Fremont factory in the summer. About 1,000 Gen 3 units are already operating on Tesla's live production floor.

"Musk tempered Optimus timeline expectations to over a year to reach the 1 million unit weekly run-rate," William Blair analyst Jed Dorsheimer said. "Early production has begun on the old Model S/X footprint in Fremont, but the critical hand and finger design are still being optimized. Data is not the bottleneck; real-world reps on open-ended tasks are. Musk noted the first applications will be in dangerous industrial applications by the end of 2027, and reaching people's homes sometime after. We think this was appropriately cautious and reinforces our view that Optimimus can remain important to the multiple well before it has meaningful impact on estimates."

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

articles.title: KFC switches to Coke. But Pepsi’s still king at Taco Bell
articles.summary: KFC dumped PepsiCo last week, but its sister chain Taco Bell announced Thursday it’s keeping the Mountain Dew Baja Blast maker on for another decade.
articles.body:
KFC dumped PepsiCo last week, but its sister chain Taco Bell announced Thursday it's keeping the Mountain Dew Baja Blast maker on for another decade.

The Taco Bell deal is a much-needed win for PepsiCo, whose business has had rough few weeks. Not only did it lose its longstanding contract with KFC to rival Coca-Cola, but its drink business in North America is also in a slump.

The company reported a 2% decline for its North America beverage unit during its most recent quarter, and its CEO Ramon Laguarta bluntly said on its earnings call that it's "not competing well in soft drinks," including newly acquired Poppi brand.

Losing the KFC contract is a blow for PepsiCo, considering it once owned the fried chicken chain. But keeping Taco Bell is a bigger deal, since the latter has generated $17 billion in US system-wide sales last year compared to KFC's roughly $5 billion. (Both chains are owned by Yum! Brands.)

Taco Bell and PepsiCo said in a statement that the two will continue collaborating on new beverages and foods until 2036, including upcoming new flavors for their Doritos Locos Tacos. It also noted that the Baja Blast drink has become a $1 billion brand.

As food prices rise and consumers look to cut back, the beverage category is a key growth area for Taco Bell and other fast food chains.

Taco Bell is aggressively expanding its beverage sales aiming to generate $5 billion in revenue by 2030. Last year, the chain released a lineup of "Refrescas" drinks aimed at attracting consumers searching for a beverage between meals. Further expansion will come from developing new Baja Blast options with Pepsi, including a limited-time pink lemonade with singer Olivia Rodrigo.

"Taco Bell's Baja Blast lineup has often been a key differentiator for the brand, and leaning into product exclusives can help drive visitation to quick service restaurant chains," Elizabeth Lafontaine, director of research at location analytics firm Placer.ai, previously told CNN.

"Especially as the industry faces steeper competition and consumers who are on the hunt for more value from fast food offerings," she added.

Taco Bell and PepsiCo said in a statement that they plan to stay ahead on "emerging beverage trends across crafted, functional and energy beverages, including energy offerings designed to appeal to Gen Z consumers and unlock new morning and afternoon occasions."

Taco Bell has been a bright spot in the fast food industry, but saw a traffic decline over the summer due toa cyclospora outbreak that was linked to lettuce served at a number of restaurants. The company will give a fuller view of the sales impact when it releases earnings next month.

articles.title: Mortgage rates dropped for the first time in months
articles.summary: The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was 7.32% this week.
articles.body:
Mortgage rates fell for the first time in over two months, though they remain not far off from multiyear highs.

The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was 7.32% this week through Wednesday, down from 7.4% a week earlier, according to Freddie Mac data.

Treasury yields, which mortgage rates closely track, eased slightly this week as investors fled to safe-haven assets amid growing political and economic unrest in Europe.

Despite very slight rate relief, home buyers are staying on the sidelines. Mortgage applications for new home purchases dropped 7% through Friday from a week earlier, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association.

"The housing market continues to face significant headwinds as elevated mortgage rates and affordability pressures keep many prospective buyers on the sidelines," MBA president and CEO Bob Broeksmit said in a statement.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS biz as shares; 30,000 certificates affected
articles.summary: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS certificate business after weak-key incident; 30,000 certificates affected, shares slide 36% as CERT-In flags flaw.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Shares of digital trust company eMudhra plunged 20% on BSE for the second consecutive day on Thursday after the company announced its decision to voluntarily exit the global SSL/TLS (Secure Sockets Layer/Transport Layer Security) certificate business following a security incident involving eight of its intermediate certificate authorities.The company’s board decided to withdraw from the business after reviewing its commercial prospects and the scrutiny triggered by the incident. The global SSL/TLS business contributes about 1% of eMudhra’s revenue, but rising compliance requirements, increasing costs and competition from free certificate providers have reduced its potential returns, the company said.“The scrutiny was disproportionate to the revenue contribution of the business,” Kaushik Srinivasan, co-founder of eMudhra, told TOI, explaining the board’s decision. He said the board met on Thursday to assess the business’s future following the incident and the sharp fall in the company’s share price over the past two sessions.Investors were bearish on the eMudhra stock after the cyber incident. In two sessions since the incident, its stock price has crashed 36% to Rs 345 by Thursday’s close, from Rs 539 at Monday’s close.The issue was reported on Oct 17 by Dennis Jackson, a member of Mozilla’s cryptography engineering team, who flagged weaknesses in the keys associated with the eight eMudhra intermediate certificates.Srinivasan said the economics of the business were becoming less attractive as certificate validity periods shortened. “The return on investment, considering the effort, investment and compliance requirements, is becoming less attractive. It makes more sense to strengthen and invest in our enterprise solutions business, which has higher margins and greater potential,” he said.The incident stems from a key-generation process conducted on April 30, 2025. Srinivasan said delays in procuring hardware for North American operations meant the company had to generate keys in India and subsequently export them. A script error resulted in weak keys, while inadequate maker-checker controls contributed to the problem.“It was a script error and human error,” he said, adding that the company would strengthen operational and security controls and review its processes.The company said it revoked the affected intermediate certificate authorities within 14 hours of discovering the issue and disclosed it promptly. Chairman V Srinivasan said the incident did not involve a compromise of the company’s infrastructure or a data breach, and that physical and logical security controls remained intact.The incident has also affected customers relying on eMudhra’s G3 root, a top-level certificate authority that helps browsers establish trust in digital certificates used to authenticate websites and secure connections.Kaushik Srinivasan said around 30,000 certificates associated with the G3 root were affected after it was distrusted, and the company was working to transition them. One customer in North America was impacted, he said.The company is working with browser programmes and customers to manage the transition. It plans to replace affected certificates and use alternative providers where required, while seeking to minimise disruption to customer-facing services.“Our G1 root, as I understand it, continues to be trusted,” Srinivasan said, adding that the company was also working to transition customers covered by the G1 root. The company has said its G1 RSA roots will continue to serve customers until the transition is complete and that replacement certificates will be provided free of cost through partners.Srinivasan said the company would commission an independent review by an empanelled auditor to examine its cryptographic keys, key inventories and key-generation processes. The findings will be made public, he said.eMudhra plans to focus on its other businesses, including digital signature certificates, eSign, enterprise public key infrastructure platforms, its emSigner eSignature Suite, and identity and authentication solutions. The company said these operations run on infrastructure separate from its global SSL/TLS business and remain unaffected.While the direct revenue contribution from SSL/TLS is small, Srinivasan said the company was also seeking to contain the reputational risk arising from the incident and restore customer confidence.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), in an advisory issued on Wednesday, said eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities were affected by a key-generation flaw that resulted in weak cryptographic private keys.You use AI every day. articles.title: Elon Musk makes $1 billion investment in Ellison’s Skydance
articles.summary: Skydance has tapped equity investments from an array of sources, including Middle East sovereign wealth funds.
articles.body:
Elon Musk has invested roughly $1 billion in Skydance, according to people familiar with the matter, providing a much needed financial injection as the company looks to cut costs and bolster its stock price.

The deal came together at roughly the same time as equity investments from Skydance's other investors, including board member Laurene Powell Jobs, the people said. Semafor reported in September that Paramount was considering seeking an equity injection from Musk.

Musk has publicly praised the Ellisons and Skydance, prompting speculation of a more expansive partnership between Musk's lower-earth-orbit satellite network, Starlink, and Skydance.

"He's gonna have to re-engineer all of those channels, and figure out how they morph into streams themselves rather than just traditional linear," billionaire cable executive John Malone said Tuesday. "I think there's a deal coming there," Malone also said at his Paley Center appearance .

"Who helped Elon finance Twitter when he bought it? Larry Ellison," Malone said. "How did Larry Ellison come up with some of the money to put into the creation of Skydance? Tesla stock. And I would not doubt for a minute that before very long you're going to see an announcement."

A deal, in fact, had already come. Ellison, who poached Mattel's Ynon Kreiz to serve as co-CEO, could use Musk's capital to bolster the company's cost-cutting and technological efforts.

"We are building a true product and tech team," Ellison said in a CNBC interview earlier this month. "We are a big believer that artificial intelligence is a tool for artists, not the other way around."

Musk and Paramount did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Musk was among a number of wealthy individuals that Paramount CEO David Ellison was considering working with for an investment.

Musk and David Ellison's father, Oracle founder Larry Ellison, have long been close, and it is in part the elder Ellison's money — and connections — that made Paramount's takeover of Warner Bros. possible. Larry Ellison has personally guaranteed more than $40 billion of the equity financing for Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros.

Larry Ellison invested $1 billion in Musk's 2022 deal to take X, formerly Twitter, private. He also invested in Tesla in 2018, and served on the company's board of directors for years.

articles.title: Big companies are rethinking 'out of control' AI spending — and turning to cheaper models
articles.summary: Companies are watching their artificial intelligence spending, and the big AI developers are catering to that.
articles.body:
IBM ( IBM ) is calling attention to a growing trend among companies and their AI spending: They're keeping a closer eye on it.

"I think what we are seeing is that at least larger enterprises are becoming a lot more cognizant and a lot more aware of what the true ROI of all of their AI spend is," IBM CEO Arvind Krishna said during the tech company's earnings call on Wednesday.

"They are also getting worried if some of the AI spending is completely out of control with no real return," he added.

While hyperscalers have been ramping up capital spending on AI infrastructure and data centers, enterprise customers are increasingly turning to open-weight models , whose core components are public, as a more cost-effective way to implement AI.

"Our computation is that for an average large enterprise, you can get going with maybe two or three racks [of infrastructure]," said Krishna. "It gives you the ability to run those open-weight models currently, anywhere from 25% to 10% of the token cost of the frontier models."

Krishna noted that IBM's on-premises IT infrastructure is well-positioned for the shift, enabling the protection of intellectual property by running models locally or on private clouds.

Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk recently argued that the key metric defining the AI build-out isn't physical capacity or power, but the price customers are willing to pay for the computing power being built. The costs of AI tokens have also fallen sharply.

(Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)

Companies are willing to pay a premium for computing power if it helps them increase revenue, improve profit margins, or cut costs. But those benefits have yet to materialize at a meaningful scale, Sløk has argued.

Frontier AI developers OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) and Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) are responding to enterprise demand for more affordable models.

OpenAI introduced lower-cost mid-range additions to its GPT-6 model family in September. Earlier this month, Anthropic unveiled Claude Haiku 5.5 , promising better performance at a lower cost than its predecessor.

Anthropic is on the march toward its highly anticipated initial public offering IPO w ith an S-1 filing potentially dropping as soon as Friday.

Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq tumble as oil climbs, investors weigh Meta, Tesla earnings
articles.summary: Stocks tumbled as oil prices surged and investors digested the latest earnings from Meta and Tesla.
articles.body: US stocks fell on Thursday, led by the Tech (XLK) sector as the AI trade unwound and Wall Street assessed earnings from EV maker Tesla (TSLA) and social media giant (META). Investors flocked to bonds, sending Treasury yields lower as oil prices surged to a five-month high.The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) declined 0.2%, while the S&P 500 (^GSPC) fell 1.2%. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) tumbled 2.1% as semicondcutor stocks fell, reversing gains from Wednesday's session. Meta shares tanked as investors weighed the company's quarterly results and 2-for-1 stock split announcement. Tesla shares were volatile after an earnings beat, as investors weighed lower 2026 capex against higher spending in 2027 and 2028 on Optimus, Cybercab, and Terafab. SpaceX (SPCX) stock fell, giving back more than half of Wednesday's post-earnings gain.Meanwhile, Blackstone's (BX) stock climbed 5% after the firm offered an upbeat outlook for its upcoming investment sales. A report that the US and Israel are preparing for renewed attacks on Iran after the US mid-term elections sent Brent crude (BZ=F) to $112 per barrel while West Texas Intermediate crude (CL=F) climbed to $100. A deadly attack at a Saudi Arabian airport and oil field also put upward pressure on energy prices. In other news, jobless claims fell to 194,000 last week, the fewest in three months, underscoring how layoffs remain low.
